pr_title: Ensure profiling is single threaded and that knn profiling occurs in the same threadpool
pr_body:
Profiling is not threadsafe. We cannot access any profiling objects between threads. 

Consequently, when profiling we should only execute over a single slice. 

Additionally, knn rewriting will not only create weights, but will also execute queries. Splitting this between two threadpools is problematic for profiling. This commit forces knn rewrite to be on the search worker thread when profiling is enabled.


closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104235
closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104131

comments:
OK, with how kNN does pre-filtering, our profiling there is just busted. 

One of the key issues is here: https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/AbstractKnnVectorQuery.java#L76

We are already profiling the weight rewriting at the top level kNN action. However, we then are rewriting the prefilter, which fires this again:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/94f2b6f1048405582185d153d1f2ca94a0118033/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/internal/ContextIndexSearcher.java#L197

So, we trip the assertion as one rewrite for this profiler is already in flight (the kNN rewrite) and then we rewrite the prefilter. 

In production, this manifests itself as incorrect rewrite values. But I wonder if how we handle this profiling is part of the issue with the original IOOBE.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104235 Recreates the issue, but its not 100% reliable. Sometimes it passes.

While debugging during a failed run, I got a warning from intellij that one of my watched variables was updated from another thread and skipped my breakpoint! Which is weird, as multi-threaded search should be turned off during profiling. 

The failure is always within the `createWeight` phase. I don't know any `createWeight` actions that are actually multi-threaded. I am still digging into this as we are definitely running into something weird with kNN prefilters & profiling.

//CC @javanna FYI

OK, I added a check to make sure the currentThread when constructing the profiler is the same thread when using it, and it turns out it isn't. I am guessing we haven't turned off multi-threading when profiling is turned on?

```
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Profiler is not thread-safe and can only be used from the thread that created it. Current thread: elasticsearch[node_s0][search_worker][T#3], profiler thread: elasticsearch[node_s0][search][T#4]
```
This is a multi-threaded search bug. We should not be using search workers and multi-threaded search when `profile: true`. Apparently we still are.

Whenever this is fixed, the following test needs to be unmuted: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104235

I believe https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/AbstractMultiTermQueryConstantScoreWrapper.java#L174  is what you were looking for, that is the cause for createWeight being called concurrently. It's not so common, but it may happen when using multi term queries. Nothing wrong with it per-se, as long as profiling is disabled, or it will blow up due to concurrent access to the profile tree which is not thread-safe.

Collections.singletonList?

The TaskExecutor has a protection mechanism to verify that a certain operation being run on the executor is not further parallelized using additional threads from the executor, as that could cause a deadlock. With that I am not sure whether calling search directly on the executor would work. Wouldn't the search offload the single slice execution to the executor, and wouldn't that fail?

> Wouldn't the search offload the single slice execution to the executor, and wouldn't that fail?

I honestly don't know. The tests pass with this change. What can we test to ensure this is protected?

I am unfamiliar with all the task parallelism code. I just know the way it currently is (profiling & parallel) is broken :)

The protection mechanism works fine and that is what prevents issues: https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/main/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/TaskExecutor.java#L147 . If it detects that we are already within the executor , we won't fork further but rather call `Runnable#run` on the current thread. Sorry about the confusion, we are good.

I opened #108041 with a fix to the profile code. I also understood why your stop-gap fixed worked: by using the search workers executor to execute the search, you implicitly disable parallelism, because task executor will detect that it's already within the executor itself and will refuse to parallelize further.
